# `parameter-added-required`

New required parameter

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `parameter-added-required` (all locations), `query-parameter-added-required`, `header-parameter-added-required`, `cookie-parameter-added-required`. Path parameters use `parameter-added-required`. |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Parameters ([RULES.md section 4](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new required query, header or cookie parameter. (Path parameters change the path; see `operation-path-changed`.)

## Why this default

Old clients don't send it, so their requests are rejected.

## Example

From test case [`parameter-added-required`](../../test/cases/parameter-added-required/): A new required query parameter.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
      get:
        operationId: listPets
-       parameters: []
+       parameters:
+       - name: limit
+         in: query
+         required: true
+         schema:
+           type: string
        responses:
          '200':
```

Findings:

- `query-parameter-added-required` · error · GET /pets

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  parameter-added-required: error
```

## How to fix

Make the parameter optional with a server-side default.
